I liked that the system was able to identify that I wanted to have sentences that mentioned what the character's were saying. I would also like if the system could recommend how I can merge these sentences with other already written sentences, or recommendations for sentence transitions.

I would suggest that the system automatically offers suggestions periodically if it notes the person is thinking or not actively typing. I think it saves time and effort from the writer who has to press tab at certain moments of the writing process, which may or may not offer suggestions.

I would like if I could see past suggestions, or a history of given suggestions. That way I could compare and contrast them, to see which ones better fit the story I had written. Some suggestions seemed better implemented in my story after writing a couple of sentences, others could be inserted with minimal transitions.

I think there should be more care in the suggestions provided, to avoid repetition or the system repeating information in the sentences it offers as suggestions. Namely, some suggestions I got repeated the word wolf a couple of times in a sentence, it could be altered to make more cohesive sense in my story. Other suggestions could have parts removed to make it more simple and less confusing, due to repeated information.

I think it would help me flesh out the story if the system offered me suggestions that also mentioned replies being made by the characters. For example, the system would offer a suggestion of what a character said, and I would have to type the reply in turn. It would help if the system also typed out the beginning of a response with such type of suggestions, that I can add to.

I think the system should offer more relevant dates, other than the dates that I have already inputted. It mentioned the date I wrote earlier, but I think it should have suggested a later date, specifically once that was set 50 years later (2137) to better match the events of the story, and that I can easily integrate without compromising the pace of the story.

I think it is good that the system takes into account a number that I had written, specifically in the context of the story 6 forms, and that the suggestions it gives is consistent with previously mentioned information. I think however it does not need to repeat such information, given how it makes the story feel repetitive if the suggestion is implemented.

The suggestions towards the end while I was trying to conclude my story seemed to be to similar to what I had written previously, specifically better suited for a story opening. It would be better if the story could identify I was trying to write a conclusion, and offer me several suggestions on how I can conclude the story.

Towards the end, the system did not provide me as much suggestions for my essay, it produced no suggestions at all unlike the beginning of my story in which it could offer me ideas on what to add to my story, or what ideas I could flesh out. I think the system when it can't find relevant suggestions to my recent sentences, should offer less general suggestions or previous suggestions, that I may use to get ideas on what to write or incorporate in the essay.

I like that the suggestions offered by the system varied in sentence length and or composition. It made my story feel active and engaging, as opposed to repetitive and having each sentence too similar to each other. It would be good if the suggestions continued to have varying sentence composition, with some being more incomplete while others being complete sentences that I can integrate in the story.

The way the suggestions start the sentence can be more varied, especially if I use a particular suggestion already in the story. I had inserted a suggestion into my story, that began with " Now, 100 years later," and a new suggestion I was given also had a similar beginning. That new suggestion had parts that I wanted to integrate, so if the suggestions would omit the repetitive parts, I could spend less time modifying the suggestion so it makes sense in the context of the story.

I think towards the end the story could not provide me suggestions, and despite adding more to the story, it was unable to determine any suggestions to give to me that I can use for the story. I think in those instances, the system should give past suggestions or a more general suggestion regarding the topic I am writing about, or even some ideas on how I can conclude the story.

The system recommended me good ideas to flesh out certain plot points that I was currently writing about. However, I think it would be good if the system tried to avoid making suggestions that reiterates past information, or regards plot points that are too similar to what already happened in the story (i.e another war/battle breaks out when too little survivors are left).

For the second paragraph, when I wanted to get a suggestion on how to start it, I got some suggestions that were odd and irrelevant. It brought up past dates, and I believe a magazine title that was not used in the story. I did find a relevant suggestion among those odd suggestions which I used, but I think in those instances, the suggestions should be relevant on the story, and not utilize outside sources or information that doesn't quite work with the plot of the story I am writing.

I think it was useful that the system offered me suggestions for starting new paragraphs in the story, such as mentioning the age of the protagonist. I think it helps with the story, and I think such repetition is useful, as opposed to other cases where it might not be effective in engaging with the readers. I think more instances should be seen in the suggestions it offers, but it should still offer alternative paragraph starters that differ from past ones to give the writer more choices if they think writing something different is more appealing for their story.

The system suggested ideas that seemed to reintroduce conflicts or plot points that would have been more useful near the beginning of my story, before I committed myself towards a specific conflict. I think when writing a conclusion or the climax of a conflict, the system should offer me suggestions that doesn't reintroduce conflicts (such as a war breaking out or chaos erupting), and instead help me make a more definite resolution for the story.

The system would tell me suggestions that reiterated specific words, such as skeptical, for emphasis on traits regarding a character. I think that works for a couple sentences I write in the story, especially if they were suggestions. However, the system should offer other ways to say the same trait for a character, synonyms for words such as skeptical when giving suggestions after the word has been used a couple times already.

I received a suggestion from the system that I thought would best be used as an ending or conclusion, so I integrated it into the essay. However, the system then would not offer me any more suggestions regarding the parts of the essay I was still working on. I think the system should have a way to either save suggestions for later, or to offer suggestions based on where I am currently writing or the previous words, and not what words are shown after it.

Some suggestions offered to me were more informative pieces of information, based on the real world. For example, suggestions were given that stated the antagonist of the game Angry Birds, and another that listed the current value of gold per weight. These suggestions aren't useful to implement in a fictional story, as opposed to other suggestions which are less based on the real world and more in the fictional world I am writing about.

I think the system should give suggestions that vary in how the sentence starts. After I wrote a sentence that started with "However," the system would give me more suggestions that included that particular word. I think if certain sentence starts such as "However" or "But" were already used recently, further suggestions should avoid sounding similar to make the story more engaging, and less repetitive.

The system recommended me suggestions that were topics or novel information that were somewhat related to bees, such as a popular game that relates to a queen bee giving orders. I think these are not as useful and more situational, it would be harder to implement in the story that is based on actual bees. Instead suggestions based on reality or accurate information should be more based on the actual topic, in this case like the behavior of bees or their hierarchy.

It was good to receive suggestions on years or dates to show the progression of the events of the story. I would like that there was more variety regarding the suggestions on how much time has passed, such as saying 2 weeks later or 30 days later, instead of only saying it is many years later or giving a new date in the form of years.

I think it would be helpful if the suggestions that were quotes or what characters say in the story would also have more information associated with it. That is that such suggestions would also include a follow up or additional words spoken by the character, or a response that another character says when they hear the sentence. I think that could help me better write out the story, with potentially less time being taken in setting up the relevant sentences.

It would be good if the system would save some recommendations for me, or give me an option to restate past suggestions it offered to me. Sometimes I received multiple suggestion in one go that I thought could all be implemented with some effort on my behalf, but I had to commit to only one at that moment, having the others potentially no longer a possibility for future suggestions.

I think the system suggesting me years is a good thing for this topic, it helps me show progression of events. However, I think the system should vary in how much time has progressed from the initial date. Many of the suggestions it takes is not a long period of time, such as 1 year. I would like at times for it to recommend me suggestions that suggest hundreds of years of passed, or even thousands in the context of the essay topic.

I think it would be good if the system could give me suggestions on other ways I can start the story, based on the topic. It would help me get ideas of what plot points can occur, and save me time on thinking of something that is different than the already inputted story, which would then help me write the rest of the story.

Some suggestions offered by the system while relevant, could not be implemented in my essay based on format. The system offered me title of chapters or what the next paragraph would deal about, but that would be better suited for a book format as opposed to the essay I was writing. In those instances, the suggestions could be reformatted or reworded to sound less like a title, and more like a opening sentence for a new paragraph.

Near the end as I was finishing up the story, the system offered me suggestions that were not quite relevant to the context of a story. Specifically, it described a board game based on the story, and mentioned some suggestions on how the game would play out. These suggestions are difficult to implement in a fiction story, considered how some were  instructions on how to play.

The system offered many suggestions to me that were relevant to my story plot, however for some of the events in the story, I would like if the system could give me more types of explanations or quotes from the characters I had written. I think that would have been a good change of pace to have the characters voice out loud their thoughts, and suggestions from the system would have helped me think of what the characters could say in the story.

The system kept offering me suggestions that was not consistent with the format or perspective I was trying to write. The suggestions were telling a story from the perspective of the reincarnation, not a past incarnation that was watching their life on the screen. While those suggestions would be helpful for a different type of story based on the topic, they were inconsistent with the narrator and perspective of the story I was writing.

I think the suggestion work well when they follow the format on how the main character thinks, in regards to their interactions in life. The suggestions should also consider what pronouns the character is using, to avoid having a conflict between what has been said about the character, (i.e stating the character is a girl or using the pronoun "he" when the character has not been given a gender or it wasn't mention at all in the story).

The system initially offered me good suggestions that I could implement and that were relevant to my story, especially as I wrote the next events of the plot. However, towards the end it stopped giving me suggestions. I had to write some more sentences, which took a bit more effort until it then was able to give me suggestions, which I then used in the story. I think the system would ideally be more consistent in the suggestions it offers, giving at least something each time I ask for them so I can get ideas on what next to write for the story.

The suggestions helped me flesh out my story and could be well integrated into the essay with minimal effort to reword some parts. I think the some suggestions that were not as effective were the ones that did not match some information I had in the essay already,  such as the mug itself, the family of John, or events that had already happen. It would have contradicted the story if used and make the essay slightly more confusing to read.

I liked that the system was able to implement information that was critical to the story in its suggestions, namely the name of the country that was fictional (Prestonia). It helps me keep the story consistent, even if the events of the story are a fictional telling of past events. However, some suggestions were inconsistent to what information I had presented prior. Namely that the country was impoverished or had poor natural resources, when the opposite was true. I think if suggestions use information I had already written, it should take care that it does not contradict the plot points I have made, which makes the story difficult to understand.

Towards the conclusion of the story I was writing, the suggestions I received were more suited for the beginning of the story, as they were not effective or practical as a way to conclude the story. Essentially they were in the format of ,"However,..." as they brought up new plot points or ideas that essentially would have to be expanded more before concluding the story, otherwise they would be unresolved or the story would end in a much more abrupt manner.

Some suggestion broke the perspective of the story, which is intended to be from the point of view of the reader experiencing a series of events relating to reincarnation. The suggestions specifically addressed the reader outside of the story, "What do you think", or even switched perspectives, "I wrote this story from a dream", and such suggestions don't match the tone or how I am writing the story.

Some suggestions near the end of my essay were ones that brought up plot points that already happened in the story earlier, specifically fighting breaking out all over the world after the first instance had been resolved. The system should avoid repeated story points unless I specifically write as such, and instead make suggestions that either bring up new events to occur in the story, or that conclude previous events that are still ongoing.

Some suggestions were describing a different type of essay, as opposed to a creative and fictional story. For example, some were informative suggestions, describing a board game or instruction on how to play, others simply listed one word suggestions that are titles to things such as reviews. I think the system should make suggestions that primarily add to the story, and not things that are better suited for other types of written works.

I think the suggestions could go in further detail regarding certain events or occurrences it suggests. That is, if it mentions an event such as a terrorist attack, it can also give a reason why it occurred or who did it, that way I can use it as a potential idea for the story, or I can rewrite it to better match what is going to happen in the story.

I liked that the suggestions were consistent with the story I had written, none of them seemed to contradict what I had written prior. Although the only thing I would like to have improved would be to have the suggestions include more adjectives for certain items mentioned, to give suggestions on how they look or other quality to better help the reader imagine the events of the story.

I think the system should refrain from suggestions that are formatting related, as you would see in a book. Suggestions such as ,"__________" or even "Chapter 2", as these were present in my story, and would be more applicable in how a book is organized. In addition, at first suggestions were not offered, I think it was a glitch based on the message it produced. The suggestions then were working correctly by the second paragraph of my essay.

The suggestions I received were relevant to the character I was writing about, it had the correct usage of names, pronouns, and more. I would also have liked if the suggestions could also offer potential qualities or traits to the characters I am writing about, so I can get an idea on how to flesh them out better. Especially if the characters are not yet as developed, and the reader knows little about them.

I think the system should definitely continue to make suggestions that are in line with the pronouns, gender, or even identity of the characters. In my story, I refrained from listing such information for the characters, to make it seem more universal and up to the interpretation of the character. As such, the suggestions in similar kinds of stories should follow if the characters aren't listed as a specific gender or identity, and even if they are explicitly named.

column11: The system struggles to come up with any new ideas, as I write on this subject. It's understandable, because this is a very abstract thinking, kind of topic to write on. I find that the system understands the structure of my sentences and phrasing, but it can't really add much to these mystical kinds of concepts. It paraphrased a lot of it's responses to my queries, taking my previous statement and finding a new way to express the same thing. The system did really well, it's suggestions were solid. I didn't find that it was very helpful in taking the story in new directions, on this topic, but that's understandable. A lot of my part in the story was about questioning everything, and that's a concept that I have trouble with, I wouldn't expect any system to figure out things that are beyond my own comprehension. I'll keep trying to work with the system and update this comment, as I go.

It seemed to have a hard time keeping its phrases on topic. I didn't get a lot that I could use from the system this time, but that may be my own lack of focus. The topic was very abstract and difficult to write on, so the suggestions I was getting probably would have worked better if I had been working with better ideas to begin with. I was able to write a story, but I still don't think it was a very good one. I can't expect the system to do a lot better than I do, when writing about a human concept like fatherhood.

This was a really good collaboration, with the system. I don't know how good the story is, but it was a lot of fun to write. I don't have any examples of how to improve the system, based on this writing session, because I would love to work with this system, exactly the way it is, again.

The system did an admirable job of providing suggestions. Most of the suggestions were kind of an echo of what I had already written, but stated in a new way. This worked well, because when I heard the suggestions, even if they were familiar, they gave me new ideas about where to go with the story. If I have any useful suggestion at all, it would be for the system to take maybe one of the optional suggestions (it seems to average about 4 suggestions per request) and take more of a gamble by giving me back something that is a more dramatic departure from what I've already written. That way, the system can analyze what I use, from its pot luck option, and learn more about how to provide fresh content suggestions. I hope that what I'm saying is coming across as logical, I'm having trouble finding good suggestions to offer.

The system seemed to be offering suggestions based on more information than I had in the abstract prompt that I was given. It gave me a lot of suggestions, citing authorship, publishing dates, context of the story outside the bounds of the abstract. It wasn't particularly helpful to me, because I was only writing off of the prompt, and did not, or could not, consider the wider subject of the story it was taken from. I would suggest that the AI confine itself to the information given in the abstract, and to not cite any information that has not already been introduced into the story unless it is new, fresh content.

What really helped me was that when the system came up with a good, fresh suggestion, it took the story in a new direction. The system did a really good job of helping me form the story during this writing session. My suggestion right now would be to keep the system working this way, but avoid cutting and pasting directly from the abstract, because it's frustrating for the writer to hope for a suggestion and to be given reused content.

I wouldn't want anything changed about the system, the way it worked during this session. It gave me good suggestions that I hadn't thought of, which really helped me to flesh out the story. I liked its suggestions enough to let it guide a good part of the story, which I haven't done with the system in any of the other writing sessions that I've done so far. I've found good suggestions in most of them, but I still felt like I led the overall story. In this session, the system was working toward forming the story in the same way I was, it seemed anyway. It felt as though the system was offering branching possibilities in its suggestions, and that was really helpful. I would suggest that the system is most useful when it offers several branching possibilities, taken from the point of the writer's last line. Like a choose your own adventure story, the computer offers branches that the writer can take to change the direction of the story. It worked well in this session.
